title: Magnetic properties of rare earth clusters
claim: For superparamagnetic rare-earth clusters, vibrational temperature can be taken as the source temperature once deflection saturates with increasing source residence time, indicating thermal equilibrium with the source.
explanation: The Langevin relation between the measured effective moment and the internal moment requires a defined temperature. Saturation of deflection versus residence time is used as the equilibrium criterion, so T in the Langevin function is the vibrational temperature equal to the source temperature.
scope: Superparamagnetic rare-earth clusters produced in the laser-vaporization source and measured by Stern-Gerlach deflection.
conditions: Residence time set by the beam chopper; source temperatures reported in Table 1 span about 73-303 K.
caveats: This equates vibrational temperature with source temperature only after saturation. Rotational temperature is separately cooled by the expansion and is not equal to the source temperature.
